MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 4, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Repp-Loadsman, Nicklas

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, OCTOBER 7, 2024

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 7,
  2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240428; LOCATION: 67 PENINSULA CENTER,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: GREG COOKE, DRC
  ENGINEERING: A request for approval of a Precise Plan of Design (PPD-240429) for the
  reconstruction of a 4.91-acre portion of an existing commercial parking lot at the Peninsula
  Shopping Center.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240163. The proposal is for the first phase of an overall parking renovation
project at the Peninsula Center due to cracking of asphalt and concrete pavement at the site.
Senior Planner Berry stated that the concrete curbing and landscape areas will be removed and
replaced and will be similar to the existing condition and there will be no change to the size of the
sidewalk areas along the building frontages. The project will add one additional standard parking

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2024
  1
 stall for a total of 399 parking stalls in this area and there will be no change to the width of the
parking stalls. Senior Planner Berry stated that the criteria for approval of a Precise Plan of
Design have been met.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve PA-
240428 (PPD-240429) with the conditions outlined in the staff report.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if the proposal includes one additional parking stall or one stall per
aisle. Senior Planner Berry clarified that the proposal is for one additional parking stall overall.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Senior Planner Berry stated that
this is the first of four phases for this project.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICAITION NO. PA-240428  SUBJECT  TO  THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
NOES:
ABSENT: REPP-LOADSMAN, NICKLAS
ABSTAIN:

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the remaining phases of the project and if they will
come back to be considered for approval by the Planning Commission. Senior Planner Berry
stated that the applicant will be submitting additional Precise Plan of Development applications
for the remaining portions of the project scope and will receive those as they work through their
capital improvement plan.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240384; ADDRESS: 30 HARBOR SIGHT DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: KRISTI SKELTON; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240385) for a 228 square foot second
  story deck extension and a Variance (V-240386) to allow rear yard improvements within
  a designated future horse keeping area.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240384. The site has a slight descending slope from the front property line to
the rear of the residence where there is a ten-foot grade change. The existing home and front
yard will not be affected by this proposal. The overall rear yard improvements include: a new 420
SF pool house; new 235 SF trellis; new 409 SF patio; new 720 SF pool; and extend an existing
112 SF second story deck out by 8 FT creating a new 228 SF deck and reconfiguring the stairs
for better accessibility to the deck area and lower rear yard. Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated
that the Neighborhood Compatibility and Variance findings have been met.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
Resolution No. PA-240384, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

Anthony Bacoka, Harbor Sight Resident about the horse keeping area. Assistant Planner
Kawagoe clarified that the applicant proposes to build in an area that would have otherwise been
used as a horse keeping area.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the exceptional or extraordinary circumstances that
the applicant is using to request a Variance in the Horse Overlay (H Overlay) Zone. Assistant

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2024
  2
 Planner Kawagoe stated that there two seepage systems in the middle of their rear yard and
cannot build in that area. Additionally, they have a smaller lot compared to neighboring lots in the
area.

Director Naughton added that there are no other horse keeping areas in the vicinity and there is
no equestrian access for this property. She stated that there was discussion to remove the horse
overlay from this neighborhood and others, during the General Plan update process, since they
do not have horse keeping facilities or equestrian access; however, the decision was for the horse
overlay to remain.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about any prohibitions for an ADU in this area. Director
Naughton stated that the applicant would encounter the same issues since the property has a
septic system unless they were to abandon the septic system and connect to the public sewer.

In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that the pool house
was not proposed to be an ADU.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that there
are several properties that currently do not meet the H Overlay Zone future horse keeping
provisions in this area. This property is unique in that there was never anything developed in the
rear yard and needs to go through the process of requesting a Variance whereas other properties
do not.

VICE CHAIR OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240384 ADOPTING RESOLUTION NO.
  PA-240384.

 Ayes: MEDAWAR, OLSON, SCHACHTER, ROMANELLI, YOO
 Noes:
 Absent: NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN
 Abstain:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has adopted Resolution No. PA-240384,
a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a second story deck extension and a Variance to
allow construction of a pool and pool house within a designated future horse keeping area. There
is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City Council by its own motion
may appeal this project.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI congratulated CHAIR MEDAWAR on receiving the Citizen of
Year award from the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce. He stated that CHAIR
MEDAWAR participates in and sponsors many of the city’s events. COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER added that he is a major contributor to the City’s Tracy Austin Tennis tournament.
CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he is humbled and grateful to have a very supportive community.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton stated that the City’s Annual Holiday Parade will be on December 7.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about the Vestar project. Director Naughton stated
that there was no need for an appeal and it will be going to the City Council at its meeting on
November 12, 2024.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, OCTOBER 8, 2024

CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

 12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 7:26 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, December 2, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Medawar, Chair
